title: Polybius, in Fordham's excerpt, describes the Roman destruction of Corinth
summary: Fordham's Polybius excerpt is an account of Rome's destruction of Corinth.
body: Fordham publishes Polybius on the Roman destruction of Corinth in 146 BCE. The page is one historian's account of the sack. It is not a Roman senate decree and not a Corinthian survivor's petition. The wording on the page includes: "whole of Greece. ---Pausanius, 7, 16-17; Livy, Ep. 52]. The incidents of the capture of Corinth were melancholy. The soldiers cared nothing for the works of art and the consecrated statues. I saw with my own eyes pictures thrown on the ground and soldiers playing dice on them; among them was a picture of Dionysus by Aristeides---in reference to which". The evidence label is the truth-gate ceiling for this host. The host is not on the gate's primary-text or official list, so the label is weak. The quotation is still the page's wording.
